sentences.text: Palaeocursornis is currently classified as a dubious genus of avemetatarsalian, a group that likely includes azhdarchoid pterosaurs. It belongs to the suborder Pterodactyloidea and is placed within the superfamily Azhdarchoidea and the family Azhdarchidae.

The genus Palaeocursornis was established by Kessler & Jurcsák in 1986, originally based on a type species first described as Limnornis corneti in 1984. However, this name had already been used for a curve-billed reedhaunter, an ovenbird, making the new name necessary. The valid name Palaeocursornis corneti was first mentioned in 1985 but remained a nomen nudum until the genus was officially established the following year.

Initially, the fossil was considered a flightless paleognath bird, possibly a ratite, or an ornithuromorph bird or non-avian theropod. A later re-evaluation suggested the specimen was not a femur but the humerus of a pterodactyloid pterosaur similar to Azhdarcho.
Furthermore, the bones attributed to the new taxon appeared to belong to two different species that were possibly not even closely related.
The type species listed in the Paleobiology Database is Palaeocursornis biharicus.

The fossil was found in Early Cretaceous Berriasian rocks dating to around 143 million years ago from a mine at Cornet near Oradea in northwestern Romania. The animal lived on an archipelago of volcanic and coral islands located towards the east of the Piemont-Liguria Ocean.
The time range for Palaeocursornis is from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
In 2025, Thomas and McDavid suggested that Palaeocursornis is a dubious genus of tapejaroid.
